Fast (2.5s wall for 3 max-size jobs through the whole pipeline) and package budget is trivially satisfied (14 entries, 55 KB).

But rules=[0,0,0] in the big stress — random predicates rarely produce rules. Let me construct a job that produces a LARGE number of rules to stress the rules output path (JSON with thousands of rules) and verify correctness against the reference (on a smaller universe so the reference can run).

Design for many rules: K=2, one field x domain [0..7] (universe 64), 32 predicates: p_i: x0 != i for i 0..7 and p_j: x1 != j-8 for j 8..15... we showed same-column pairs are minimal hitting sets but tautologies under cond3 (cannot jointly falsify same-column ne). Mixed structure needed.

Better idea: predicates p_i: x0 >= i for i in 0..7 (8 preds) and q_j: x1 >= j for j 0..7 (8) and r on sums... Training rows: masks. Family of masks = prefixes. Minimal hitting sets of prefix family... singletons {i} with i ≤ min over rows... few.

Alternative approach to many minimal hitting sets: family of masks = complements of disjoint-ish triples realized over a universe with actual falsifiers. Let me think about what's realizable: preds as threshold comparisons partition the universe into intervals... Simplest: use eq predicates on cell values! p_i: x0 == i (i in 0..7): 8 preds; s_j: x1 == j (j 0..7): 8 preds; t_k: x0+x1 == k... 16 preds total for k in 0..15? Sum values0..14 (15 preds) → total 31 preds. Row (a,b): mask = {x0==a} ∪ {x1==b} ∪ {sum==a+b} → exactly 3 true bits. Family of 3-bit masks. Minimal hitting sets = transversals of the hypergraph of triples (a,b,a+b): hitting sets of size ≤ 4 — transversals of ~64 triples over 31 vertices... The transversal number is 3 (choose x0==a, x1==b for one (a,b)... no that hits just rows (a,*),( *,b),(a,b) — need to hit all 64 triples: triple (a,b,s) must be hit. H hits all rows iff for every (a,b): H∋ a-pred or H ∋ b-pred or H ∋ (a+b)-pred. This is a hitting-set problem on a "sum graph". Minimal hitting sets: e.g. all x0 preds {0..7} size 8 > width. Smaller: mix... e.g. H = {x0==0, x0==1, ..., } hmm. Transversals of the triples (a,b,a+b): choose all sum preds {2,...,9} hits every row except (a,b) with a+b ∉ 2..9... always? a+b ranges 0..14. rows with a+b=0: (0,0); 1: (0,1),(1,0); 10..14: various. So not full.

This is getting complicated. Since the reference is too slow for big universes anyway, let me stress the output path directly with a synthetic test: monkeypatch? No — better to just craft the "missing-1-bit family" job which gives 496 pair rules with a universe where pairs ARE jointly falsifiable.

Missing-1-bit family: rows' masks miss exactly one bit. If predicate p_i is false exactly at universe windows with some property... For pair {i,j} to have a counterexample, need a window where both p_i and p_j false. And for row (mask missing exactly bit i) to be realizable: a window where all preds true except p_i.

Design: field x domain [0..31], K=1 (universe 32). Predicates p_i: x != i (i in 0..31). Window a: mask = all except p_a ✓ missing-1-bit family. Rows: many (duplicates of all a values). Minimal hitting sets = pairs {i,j} ✓ = 496 rules... BUT counterexample for pair {i,j}: window with x==i and x==j → impossible → tautology → excluded!! So cond3 kills them.

To have counterexamples: use two cells! x domain [0..31], y domain [0..31], universe 1024. Predicates p_i: (x != i) OR... no — predicates are atomic. Hmm: p_i: x + y !=2i? Window (a,b): p_i false iff a+b == 2i. Rows: masks missing bits {i : 2i == a+b} = missing exactly 1 bit (i=(a+b)/2 if even)... For odd sums, no bit missing (all true). Family = masks missing 1 bit + all-true. Minimal hitting sets = pairs {i,j}: counterexample = window with a+b=2i and a+b=2j → impossible again. Tautologies again!

Fundamental issue: if each row misses ≥ ... pair {i,j} falsifiable iff some window falsifies both p_i and p_j. If the falsifier sets F_i are pairwise disjoint (each window falsifies ≤ 1 pred), then NO pair has a counterexample → all rules are singletons (if any pred is non-tautological... singleton {i} falsified at F_i ≠ ∅). So with disjoint falsifier sets: rules = singletons that cover all rows = {i : F_i has no rows}? no wait — singleton {i} is a rule iff cond1: all rows satisfy p_i — i.e., no row in F_i. With rows missing bit i → row i falsifies p_i → singleton {i} fails cond1. Hmm, so with the missing-1-bit family and disjoint falsifier sets: rules = ∅!

For MANY rules with counterexamples, we need overlapping falsifier sets. E.g., windows where 3 preds are simultaneously false (rows with masks missing 3 bits) and pairs... Let me design: 32 preds; falsifier structure: universe windows w_S for various S; rows with masks missing exactly 3 bits {a,b,c} where each of a,b,c pairs... Let me think: family of masks = complements of 3-subsets (masks missing exactly 3 bits). Minimal hitting sets of size ≤ 4: H hits mask m iff H has ≥1 bit outside the missing 3-set → |H \ {a,b,c}| ≥ 1. H misses iff H ⊆ {a,b,c}. So hitting iff for every missing-triple T: H ⊄ T. Minimal hitting sets: size 1: {i}: misses T containing i → fails. size 2: {i,j}: fails T ⊇ {i,j} (exists if some row's triple contains both) → depends on triple family. size 3: {i,j,k}: fails iff {i,j,k} is a triple in family. So minimal hitting sets = all pairs {i,j} NOT both contained in any row-triple, plus all triples not in the family (if they hit... every triple hits iff it's not itself a row-triple; minimal iff all its pairs fail, i.e., each pair is contained in SOME row-triple).

Construct: rows = all windows (a,b,c) of special structure. Let universe be: field x [0..31], y [0..31] (1024 windows). Preds p_i: x != i for i in 0..15 (16 preds); q_j: y != j for j in 0..15 (16 preds). Window (a,b) falsifies {p_a (if a<16), q_b (if b<16)} — at most 2. Masks missing ≤ 2 bits. Family (rows a,b < 16): missing {p_a, q_b}. Minimal hitting sets computed earlier = same-column pairs (120+120=240 rules) but same-column pairs have no counterexample → tautologies → 0 rules. Cross pairs {p_a,q_b} fail row (a,b). So 0 rules. Grr.

Let me flip: make rows' masks missing 3 bits: preds p_i: x != i (i 0..7), q_j: y != j (j 0..7), r_k: x+y != k (k 0..15)? Window (a,b) with a,b<8: falsifies p_a, q_b, r_{a+b}: 3 bits missing. Rows = all 64 windows with a,b<8 (train rows restricted to domain... train rows must have values in domains; if domain is [0..7] both, universe = 64 windows. cond3: falsify clause H at window (a,b) means H ⊆ {p_a, q_b, r_{a+b}}... wait falsify = all literals false = H's preds all false at (a,b) = H ⊆ falseset(a,b) = {p_a,q_b,r_{a+b}}.

Rules: minimal hitting sets of the family of missing-3-bit masks = H where for all (a,b): H ⊄ {p_a,q_b,r_{a+b}} (as computed: |H \ T(a,b)| ≥ 1 where T(a,b)={p_a,q_b,r_{a+b}}... careful: H hits mask(a,b) iff H ∩ (preds \ T(a,b)) ≠ ∅ iff H \ T(a,b) ≠ ∅). So hitting iff no T(a,b) ⊇ H. Then also need falsifier: H ⊆ T(a,b) for some (a,b) — i.e., H = subset of some row-triple. And minimal.

H of size 1: {p_a}: H ⊆ T(a,b) for any b ✓ falsifier exists; hitting: need p_a ∉ ... H\T = ∅ when a'=a... wait hitting iff for all (a',b'): |H \ T(a',b')| ≥ 1: H={p_a}: H\T(a',b') = {p_a} \ {p_{a'},q_{b'},r_{a'+b'}} = ∅ iff a==a'. So {p_a} fails row (a,b') → not hitting. Similarly all singletons fail.

H size 2: e.g. {p_a, p_{a'}} with a≠a': H\T(a',b') ⊇ {p_a} when a'==a... for any (u,v): T(u,v) contains at most one p-pred → H\T ≥ 1 ✓ hitting! Falsifier: need H ⊆ T(a,b): T has one p-pred → impossible → tautology → excluded. Cross pair {p_a, q_b}: row (a,b): H ⊆ T(a,b) → H\T = ∅ → not hitting ✗. Cross pair {p_a, r_k}: rows (u,v) with u≠a: H\T ⊇ both... check all: (u,v)=(a,v): T={p_a,q_v,r_{a+v}}: H\T = {r_k} minus r_{a+v} = ∅ iff k=a+v. If k-a in domain... v=k-a with0≤v<8: then H\T=∅ → not hitting. Choose k such that no v: e.g. k=0, a=7: v=-7 invalid → rows (7,v): r_{7+v} with v≥0... k=0 ≠ 7+v ✓ hitting? Also rows (u≠7): H\T = {p_7} ∋ p_7 ✓. So {p_7, r_0} hits all ✓. Falsifier: H ⊆ T(a,b): need p_7 ∧ r_0 false together: window (7, v) with 7+v=0 → impossible! → tautology ✗ excluded. Hmm.

H size 3 = a row-triple {p_a, q_b, r_{a+b}}: hitting? H \ T(a,b) = ∅ → NOT hitting ✗.

H size 3 not a row-triple, e.g. {p_a, q_b, r_k} with k ≠ a+b: hitting iff for all (u,v): H ⊄ T(u,v) i.e. H\T(u,v) ≠ ∅: T(u,v) = {p_u,q_v,r_{u+v}}. H\T = ∅ iff {p_a,q_b,r_k} ⊆ {p_u,q_v,r_{u+v}} iff u=a, v=b, k=u+v=a+b → k≠a+b → never ✓ hitting. Minimal? Pairs: {p_a,q_b} fails row(a,b) ✓; {p_a,r_k} fails row (a, k-a) if k≥a and k-a<8... if such row exists, pair fails (not hitting) → then p... hold on minimality: H minimal iff every pair-subset is NOT a hitting set (fails some row). {p_a,q_b} fails (a,b) ✓. {p_a,r_k} fails row (a, k-a) iff k-a ∈ [0,8) i.e., a ≤ k < a+8. {q_b,r_k} fails row (k-b, b) iff k-b ∈ [0,8). Falsifier: need H ⊆ T(u,v): H={p_a,q_b,r_k} ⊆ T(u,v) requires u=a,v=b,k=a+b → contradiction with k≠a+b → NO falsifier → tautology ✗ again!!

Hmm!! Interesting: with rows = ALL windows, mask(window) = falseset complement... wait no. Hold on — I conflated. Row masks are the truth masks ON TRAINING ROWS; falseset(window) is over universe windows. In this design train rows = universe windows = all (a,b). Row (a,b) mask = preds true at (a,b) = all except {p_a,q_b,r_{a+b}} (3 missing). Clause H falsified at window (a,b) iff H ⊆ {p_a,q_b,r_{a+b}} = T(a,b). If all windows are rows (train=universe), then H is a hitting set (cond1: every row satisfies H: H ∩ mask ≠ ∅ ⇔ H ⊄ T) AND has falsifier (H ⊆ T(a,b) for some (a,b)) — contradiction! So with train == universe, rules =∅. Makes sense: cond1 + falsifier need window in universe minus train (or... "including unseen data"!). So counterexamples must come from windows NOT covered by training masks' rows.

So for many rules: train rows should NOT cover the whole universe; the falsifier windows must lie outside train. E.g., restrict train rows to a,b ∈ [0,4) (16 rows) but universe a,b ∈ [0,8): masks of rows missing triples T(a,b) for a,b<5... and falsifiers at windows with a,b ≥ 5... Falsifier of H at (u,v): H ⊆ T(u,v). For H minimal hitting set of family {T(a,b): a,b < 5}: need H ⊆ T(u,v) for some (u,v) with u or v ≥ 5...

"""Hunt many-rule jobs: tiny train, small universe, P=32, width=4."""
import ctypes, sys, json, random, time
ctypes.CDLL('/workspace/vendor/system-libs/libz.so.1', mode=ctypes.RTLD_GLOBAL)
sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace/vendor'); sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace/submission')
sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace/dev')
from netnomos.finite import compile_job
from reference import ref_compile

def gen(rng, ntrain=4, P=32, width=4, K=2, dsize=4):
    fields = [{'name': f'f{i}', 'type': ['time','size','count','id','flag'][i%5],
               'domain': list(range(dsize))} for i in range(2)]
    allrefs = [[s, f['name']] for s in range(K) for f in fields]
    preds = []
    for p in range(P):
        kind = rng.choice(['cmp','cmp','any','all'])
        if kind == 'cmp':
            left = rng.choice([{'ref': rng.choice(allrefs)},
                               {'sum': rng.sample(allrefs, rng.randint(1,3))},
                               {'scale': rng.randint(0,3), 'ref': rng.choice(allrefs)}])
            right = rng.choice([{'ref': rng.choice(allrefs)},
                                {'const': rng.randint(0,5), 'type':'count'}])
            preds.append({'kind':'cmp','left':left,'op':rng.choice(['eq','ne','lt','le','gt','ge']),'right':right})
        else:
            f = rng.choice(fields)
            preds.append({'kind':kind,'field':f['name'],'op':rng.choice(['eq','ne','lt','le','gt','ge']),
                          'value':rng.randint(0,5)})
    train = [[[rng.randrange(dsize) for f in fields] for _ in range(K)] for _ in range(ntrain)]
    queries = [{'target':[0,fields[0]['name']],'prefix':rng.choice(['','0','3']),'fixed':[]} for _ in range(4)]
    return {'fields':fields,'slots':K,'predicates':preds,'width':width,'train':train,
            'approved':[],'queries':queries}

def main():
    seed=int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv)>1 else 0
    rounds=int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv)>2 else 200
    rng=random.Random(seed)
    best=0; bestjob=None
    for r in range(rounds):
        job=gen(rng)
        t0=time.perf_counter()
        out=compile_job(job)
        dt=time.perf_counter()-t0
        nr=len(out['rules'])
        if nr>best:
            best=nr; bestjob=job
            print(f'round {r}: rules={nr} time={dt:.3f}s')
    # cross-check the biggest one against the naive reference
    if bestjob:
        t0=time.perf_counter()
        ref=ref_compile(bestjob)
        dtr=time.perf_counter()-t0
        eng=compile_job(bestjob)
        print('cross-check:', 'OK' if ref==eng else 'MISMATCH', f'ref_time={dtr:.2f}s')
        # also serialize large output through main.py
        import subprocess, os
        env=dict(os.environ); env['NETNOMOS_DEPS']='/workspace/vendor'
        proc=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-I','-B','/workspace/submission/main.py'],
                            input=json.dumps({'jobs':[bestjob]}),capture_output=True,text=True,env=env,timeout=60)
        got=json.loads(proc.stdout)
        assert got=={'results':[ref]}, 'pipeline mismatch'
        print('pipeline large-output OK; rules =', best)
    print('max rules seen:', best)

if __name__=='__main__':
    main()
PYEOF
